executive_assessment.text: Ukraine faces increasing heat, drought, seasonal water imbalance, flood, and wildfire pressures, but much of the physical baseline predates the full-scale invasion and does not reflect war-altered land, population, monitoring, and infrastructure systems.

The principal current Climate-FCV interaction runs from conflict to climate vulnerability: war damage, displacement, contamination, mines, and access constraints weaken energy, water, agriculture, ecosystems, services, and future adaptation.

Municipal planning, emergency coping, climate-informed reconstruction options, and area-based recovery provide capacity, while independent evaluation shows environmental, inclusion, staffing, finance, and monitoring trade-offs.

coverage.gap_note: Most physical evidence predates war-altered exposure and monitoring.
Irrigation evidence is concentrated in damaged southern and eastern systems.
Most evidence concerns participation and recommended design rather than outcomes.
Official national synthesis cannot describe every current municipality.
Independent performance evidence is localized to Mykolaiv.
Only the weather-energy interaction is directly observed; longer-term chains remain inferred.
Local recovery capacity is documented without causal peace outcomes.

coverage.value: Heat, drought, flood, wildfire, and changing seasonal pressures
War-damaged energy, water, agriculture, land, and infrastructure systems
Environmental contamination, ecosystem damage, and climate vulnerability
Displacement, municipal services, and differentiated vulnerability

Evaluated response effectiveness and unintended effects
coverage.gap_note: Evidence is localized and lacks counterfactual climate or peace evaluation.

geographic_notes.text: National assessments are complemented by evidence from southern and eastern agricultural and water systems, the Lower Dnipro, combat-affected forests, government-controlled cities, frontline and host municipalities, and Mykolaiv; these findings have different territorial and access coverage.
Occupied, frontline, recently retaken, return, host, rural, and smaller-municipality conditions are not comparably observed, and national totals systematically carry access and classification gaps.

sector_notes.text: Agriculture, water, energy, housing, municipal services, ecosystems, displacement, forestry, health, and education are represented; private-sector adaptation, coastal risk, transport resilience, and national social-protection performance remain thin.

known_gaps.text: Ukraine lacks an integrated, current, high-resolution climate baseline that reflects war-altered land, population, infrastructure, hydrology, monitoring coverage, and occupied-territory uncertainty.

Independent response evaluation is localized to Mykolaiv; climate-integrated reconstruction, municipal adaptation, displacement integration, ecosystem recovery, and unintended distributional effects remain largely unevaluated.

The fcv-to-climate reverse pathway is well supported qualitatively through infrastructure, access, displacement, and environmental damage, but its additional effect on future climate losses and adaptation performance is not quantified.
Territorially comparable evidence disaggregated by gender, age, disability, displacement status, livelihood, and occupied or frontline location remains incomplete.
